name: Symphyotrichum

project_scope.selection_mode: live 2026-10-12 manifest audit; historical B071 comparisons preserved
project_scope.native_range_note: Installed learner membership does not override scientific native-range HOLD/FAIL.

shared_traits: Asteraceae heads consist of disk and often ray florets with enclosing phyllaries.
Compare leaf bases, hairs/glands, phyllaries, flowering arrangement and growth habit on the SAME plant.
Small white heads or lavender rays alone do not prove species.
priority: Start annual vs perennial and inspect whole flowering array; inland narrow-leaved annual DIVARICATUM is not Eurybia white wood aster.
Inspect leaf TEXTURE: stiff spinulose heath leaves (ericoides) or silvery appressed hairs (sericeum).
Compare upper leaf BASES: deeply heart-clasping patens vs oblong to weakly clasping oblongifolium. Glands may occur in BOTH.
Compare lower leaf petiole wings and peduncle hairs: hairy drummondii vs glabrous-peduncled eulae (often 27–36 rays).

For tall wet-site praealtum/lanceolatum, inspect BOTH leaf faces: praealtum usually firm waxy/revolute with well-defined small isodiametric areoles underneath; lanceolatum typically more pliable/nonwaxy with fainter elongated areoles. The FNA genus key and species accounts CONFLICT on bract counts; do not use counts as primary distinction.
For S. lanceolatum nominate, compare outer/inner phyllaries: usually outer 1/3–2/3 length of inner; do not confuse subsp. hesperium; keep range UNRESOLVED.
Reserve arrows for photo-verified anatomical details; keep scientific range FAIL/UNRESOLVED where recorded.
study_strategy.warning: Historical genus summary said eight installed, but live manifest has ten. Most important prior ERROR was calling S. divaricatum 'white woodland aster' (Eurybia divaricata); the Symphyotrichum divaricatum species card has now been corrected. Also do not teach glands as exclusive to S. oblongifolium: S. patens varieties can have stalked glands.

curation_status.comparison_state: ALL TEN INSTALLED TAXA HAVE MORPHOLOGY-FIRST GENUS ROUTING; 6 lookalike lessons first-pass complete; targeted diagnostic photo and taxonomic holds remain

b071_study_strategy.warning: Symphyotrichum IDs are easy to over-simplify from flower color. Use vegetative characters, stem hair, leaf architecture, habitat, and current variety/subspecies names together.

quick_split: S. eulae — Texas endemic; scabrous serrate leaves, open panicle, white to pale lavender rays.
S. drummondii var. texanum — larger serrate lower leaves with winged petiole-like bases, much smaller upper leaves, short-hairy stems.
S. ericoides var. ericoides — many tiny stiff narrow leaves, short-strigose stems, masses of small white heads.
S. lanceolatum subsp. lanceolatum — tall moist-site white-panicle aster with narrow lanceolate leaves; range HOLD pending third exact target county.

scientific_diagnostic_review_20261008.review_type: morphology-first comparative lesson; preserves existing B071, scientific status and canonical membership
look_here_first: Collect lower and upper leaves from the SAME plant; note winged-petiolate versus sessile blades and degree of reduction upward.
Magnify stem and flower-stalk hairs: glabrous versus short-hairy versus stalked glandular; compare peduncle bracts.
Photograph whole flowering branch and one scaled side-view of the involucre; count ray florets where intact.
Compare phyllary shape, orientation, margins, tips and glandular hairs. Habitat and ray color are supporting evidence only.

strongest_separators: S. drummondii var. texanum: stems densely hirsute distally, winged-petiolate larger lower leaves, open panicle with long spreading branches; FNA variety treatment involucre 3.8–5.2 mm.
S. eulae: glabrous peduncles, heads with (20–)27–36 rays, hemispheric involucre (4–)5–6.5 mm; compare with S. drummondii species-level (8–)10–15(–20) rays and usually hairy peduncles.
comparison_groups.overlap_warning: Involucre size overlaps broadly, and ray number meets at about 20; flower color is variable. FNA species-level drummondii measurements and variety-specific treatments are not interchangeable. Verify specimen-level varietal determination before mapping aliases.
photo_roles: ray-floret count from intact face-on head

strongest_separators: Usually narrow, stiff, spinulose-tipped leaves, small heads with 2.5–4.5(–5) mm involucres, usually (8–)10–18(–20) rays, and spinulose-tipped phyllaries per Semple's Astereae Lab treatment.
Look for white or translucent spinules with close magnification, not simply 'sharp-looking' phyllary tips.
comparison_groups.overlap_warning: Tiny white heads, narrow leaves and pale ray color recur across asters. Some similar species have rolled phyllary edges that mimic spinules; inspect the actual tip.
photo_roles: Joey/user flowering branch if taxon identity established

comparison_groups.role: comparison reference only; absent from the eight-species installed manifest at this check
strongest_separators: Stalked glandular hairs on upper stems, peduncles and phyllary faces; rhizomatous habit, often leaflike outer phyllaries.
FNA involucres (5–)7–9 mm; stalked glandular peduncles 0.5–5 cm; inspect actual glands rather than relying on aromatic odor.
comparison_groups.overlap_warning: Purple rays, aromatic foliage, compact habit and a single involucre measurement are not diagnostic alone.

genus_diagnostics.leaf_base: Compare lower, middle and upper leaves on the SAME stem: strongly clasping, winged petiole, nearly sessile, narrow-stiff, or silvery.
genus_diagnostics.pubescence: Check hairs and stalked glands on upper stems, peduncles and phyllaries using 10–20× lens.
genus_diagnostics.flowering_head: Observe head/flower rays, side-view phyllary ranks, involucre millimeter measurement, flowering-branch architecture; ray COLOR alone is not diagnostic.
genus_diagnostics.developmental: Separate short-lived annual narrow-leaved saltmarsh asters from rhizomatous perennials; observe basal crown before inferring species.
genus_diagnostics.silky_aster: S. sericeum: first check the dense, soft, long APPRESSED WHITE HAIRS coating leaf surfaces and phyllaries, visible in two new licensed close-ups; then inspect wiry short rootstock. Compare Texas look-alike S. pratense: sparser sericeous hairs and broader ovate bracts; exclude aromatic/late purple asters by hair type and leaf base.

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Annual/short-lived; wiry nearly glabrous; narrow mostly sessile leaves 1–3.5 mm; small heads in VERY OPEN diffuse inflorescence
species_comparison_matrix.separate_from: vs S. subulatum: denser pyramid, mostly SE saline/coastal Texas; do not confuse with Eurybia divaricata, white wood aster
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: open panicle; narrow leaf with scale; involucre

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Perennial; larger serrate lower leaves taper into winged petiole; reduced narrow upper leaves; hairy stems
species_comparison_matrix.separate_from: vs S. eulae: hairy flower stalks vs often glabrous; fewer rays in published treatments; local var. texanum distinctions need checked
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: matched lower/upper leaves; hairy peduncle; full head ray count

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Dense fine-leaved upper flowering branchlets plus a TRUE white/clear stiff PHYLLARY tip spine visible at 10–20× (not a folded green tip). Typical involucre 2.5–4.5(–5) mm.
species_comparison_matrix.separate_from: S. divaricatum is an open, very diffuse, nearly hairless annual with widely spaced heads. S. pilosum (outside project) often has larger heads and curled GREEN phyllary tips that mimic actual S. ericoides spines. S. eulae broader serrate leaves, generally glabrous peduncles and more rays.
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: True phyllary apical clear bristle macro vs curled green pilosum tip; tight leaf-branchlet photo; existing Peter M. Dziuk 2003 arrowed source photo copyright study-link only

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Texas endemic; serrate scabrous leaves; spreading flower branches; glabrous peduncles; typically 27–36 rays
species_comparison_matrix.separate_from: vs drummondii: leaf petiole wings, stem hairs, peduncle hairs, ray count and involucre size together
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: peduncle hairs; ray count; leaf series

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Thin flexible flat-edged nonwaxy upper leaf surfaces, indistinct/elongate vein areoles below; confirm outer:inner phyllary ratio 1/3–2/3 for nominate infraspecific concept.

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Short oblong leaves, often low bushy rhizomatous; stalked glandular hairs on upper stems/peduncles/phyllaries
species_comparison_matrix.separate_from: vs patens: patens has strongly heart-clasping upper leaves, BUT patens can ALSO have glandular phyllaries
species_comparison_matrix.photo_need: leaf bases on stems; glands macro; phyllary face

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Strongly cordate-clasping to auriculate UPPER stem leaves; branches spreading then rising
species_comparison_matrix.separate_from: vs oblongifolium: upper leaf attachment strongest; patens varies by variety and CAN have stalked glands

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Leaves stiff/firm, often revolute edges, WAXY upper face, well-marked small near-equal-dimension underside vein AREOLES.
species_comparison_matrix.separate_from: S. lanceolatum more pliable nonwaxy foliage with less regular areoles; peduncle-bract counts contradictory in FNA key vs accounts and NOT reliable as hard split.

species_comparison_matrix.look_here_first: Actual long, fine, WHITE/SILVER hairs lying flat on both leaf surfaces, plus similarly silky phyllaries; see two new arrowed feature closeups by davecz2.
species_comparison_matrix.separate_from: S. oblongifolium has rougher/narrower leaves and often glandular upper shoots; S. pratense of Texas has much less dense hairy leaves and broadly ovate phyllaries — comparison only.

quick_key.if: Annual/short-lived; wiry nearly glabrous; narrow mostly sessile leaves 1–3.5 mm; small heads in VERY OPEN diffuse inflorescence
Perennial; larger serrate lower leaves taper into winged petiole; reduced narrow upper leaves; hairy stems
Perennial; many tiny stiff pointed leaves and white small heads; spinulose phyllary tips
Small mostly white asters with bracts that SEEM spiny but show a GREEN rolled or incurved phyllary tip (no separate clear/white stiff bristle), often larger heads than heath aster
quick_key.then: Check Symphyotrichum pilosum — COMPARISON ONLY, not currently canonical; true S. ericoides has a pale/clear apical spine.

quick_key.if: Texas endemic; serrate scabrous leaves; spreading flower branches; glabrous peduncles; typically 27–36 rays
Tall wet-site perennial, thin/pliable flat-edged nonwaxy leaves; underside veins faint/irregular/elongate; nominate-subspecies outer phyllaries ~1/3–2/3 inner
quick_key.then: Symphyotrichum lanceolatum subsp. lanceolatum — RANGE HOLD. Confirm infraspecific concept with voucher; flowering bract counts DISPUTED between FNA key and species accounts.

quick_key.if: Short oblong leaves, often low bushy rhizomatous; stalked glandular hairs on upper stems/peduncles/phyllaries
Strongly cordate-clasping to auriculate UPPER stem leaves; branches spreading then rising

quick_key.if: Narrow leaves distinctly SILVER from dense appressed silky hairs; low wiry perennial with woody crown
Narrow-leaved annual of SE saline Texas; relatively dense PYRAMIDAL flowering array

central_texas_look_here_first: 1. Southern annual saltmarsh aster — Annual/short-lived; wiry nearly glabrous; narrow mostly sessile leaves 1–3.5 mm; small heads in VERY OPEN diffuse inflorescence
2. Texas/Drummond's aster — Perennial; larger serrate lower leaves taper into winged petiole; reduced narrow upper leaves; hairy stems
3. White heath aster — Perennial; many tiny stiff pointed leaves and white small heads; spinulose phyllary tips
4. Eula's/Whitehouse's aster — Texas endemic; serrate scabrous leaves; spreading flower branches; glabrous peduncles; typically 27–36 rays
5. White panicle aster — Tall moist-site rhizomatous plant with narrow leaves not strongly reduced upward; few stalk bracts
6. Aromatic/fall aster — Short oblong leaves, often low bushy rhizomatous; stalked glandular hairs on upper stems/peduncles/phyllaries
7. Late purple/clasping aster — Strongly cordate-clasping to auriculate UPPER stem leaves; branches spreading then rising
8. Willowleaf aster — Tall clonal rhizomatous plant with long willowlike leaves; broad panicle; possible longitudinal stem hair lines
9. Western silver/silky aster — Narrow leaves distinctly SILVER from dense appressed silky hairs; low wiry perennial with woody crown
10. True annual saltmarsh aster — Narrow-leaved annual of SE saline Texas; relatively dense PYRAMIDAL flowering array

head_to_head.first: drummondii: winged-petiolate large lower leaves, strongly smaller upper leaves, hairy distal shoots/peduncles. eulae: glabrous peduncles, open horizontal flowering branches, usually 27–36 rays.

head_to_head.pair: S. praealtum vs S. lanceolatum (including nominate subspecies)
head_to_head.first: FIRST compare 2–3 mature leaves from middle/upper stems, BOTH faces: S. praealtum has relatively FIRM leaves, often rolled-back (revolute) edges, WAXY upper faces, and lower faces with conspicuous almost equally wide/long (isodiametric) small areoles. S. lanceolatum usually has PLIABLE, flatter leaves, nonwaxy upper faces and less distinct/elongate irregular areoles. Flowering-branch bract counts overlap or conflict among FNA key vs species descriptions; NEVER a hard split.
head_to_head.trap: SOURCE DISAGREEMENT: FNA 2006 genus key couplet 84 says lanceolatum 5–12+ and praealtum 1–3(–5), but FNA species treatments report the reverse (lanceolatum 1–3[–5], praealtum 5–12+). Do not teach either count as independently diagnostic until local voucher-level confirmation. Nominate S. lanceolatum subsp. lanceolatum requires outer phyllaries usually 1/3–2/3 inner and no conspicuous big foliaceous head-subtending bract; separate var. hesperium.
head_to_head.photo: MATCHED exact identity verified leaf abaxial areole micros + adaxial wax/edge-rolling, head-side outer/inner phyllary scale; record bract counts as observations, NOT a validated binary key.

head_to_head.first: S. divaricatum: an often wiry annual with VERY OPEN diffuse flowering branches and widely separated heads, common inland. TRUE S. subulatum: relatively DENSER PYRAMIDAL upper flowering array with heads closer together nearer top, primarily southeastern Texas saline/coastal marshes. Both have narrow mostly sessile foliage; confirm on unmowed mature whole plant.
head_to_head.trap: Density is RELATIVE, not compact vs perfectly airy in every specimen: mowing, juvenile plants and disturbance can defeat the silhouette. The phyllary green-zone feature is described but hard to resolve reliably in photos. Old S. subulatum var. ligulatum goes to S. divaricatum; old Uvalde 2014 'subulatum' image is quarantined, not a verified true-subulatum photo.
head_to_head.photo: 5 physical divaricatum field/flower views, but no whole panicle positively identifying true subulatum. Historic Uvalde picture quarantined. Seek SAME-SCALE mature flowering arrays from known current taxa, then side-view phyllaries with metric scale.

head_to_head.first: S. sericeum: actual long, soft, APPRESSED SILVERY hairs covering both leaf surfaces AND phyllaries; photo macro confirmed. S. oblongifolium: more often rough short leaf hairs, glandular upper peduncles; S. patens deeply clasping leaf bases. Compare S. pratense (Texas look-alike, NOT installed): less dense silver pubescence and broader ovate phyllaries.
head_to_head.trap: Not all Texas silver-looking asters are sericeum. S. pratense can be somewhat silky but is less densely hairy and has larger, wider outer bracts. Purple rays, sunlight glare and common-name silver color are NOT species diagnoses.
